title: Red letters on a pale box
label: Brand gallery
lede: A CompUSA was a plain big-box building with the name in red capitals over the door. Here is the store as it survives in photographs and the logo as it survives in the archive, with our drawings in the same spirit.

archive.caption: The logo from the website header, with the “.com” added under Systemax.
archive.credit: Cropped from an Internet Archive capture of compusa.com. Shown for commentary; trademarks belong to their owners.

archive.caption: A store on El Camino Real in Santa Clara, California.
archive.credit: Photo: Coolcaesar at en.wikipedia, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:CompUSA_Santa_Clara_1.jpg), CC BY-SA 3.0.

archive.caption: “America’s Computer Store” with a “Store closing” banner. The photographer left only the sign in colour.
archive.credit: Photo: Terry Ross from Corpus Christi, Texas, United States, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Store_Closing_(2212179765).jpg), CC BY-SA 2.0.

archive.caption: The same store four weeks later, in a photograph its author titled “Last Seven Days.”
archive.credit: Photo: Terry Ross from Corpus Christi, Texas, United States, via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Last_Seven_Days_(2275973005).jpg), CC BY-SA 2.0.
